title: "seen, Sita"
hook: Hanuman has the biggest news of Rama's life, and he chooses his first word with care
carry: he arranges his words around Rama's fear

segments.voice: Yesterday: the return. The search party wrecked Sugriva's honey forest, and your line, a wrecked orchard, good news, is how Sugriva read it.
screen: `THE RETURN: A WRECKED ORCHARD, GOOD NEWS.`

segments.voice: Rama has been waiting on a mountain outside Kishkindha. The search parties from the north, the east and the west have already come back with nothing. Now the southern party arrives, loud and happy, and Hanuman steps forward. He has crossed the sea, found her, spoken with her, fought half of Lanka and left it burning. He has a long, astonishing story to tell. And first he has to decide which word comes out of his mouth.
screen: `A MOUNTAIN, AND NO NEWS.` → `THREE PARTIES CAME BACK EMPTY.` → `WHICH WORD FIRST?`

segments.voice: The word he puts first, in Valmiki's Sanskrit, is drishta. Seen. He bows and tells Rama the queen has been seen, that she is keeping her vows, that she is unharmed. Think about the order. If he had begun with the ocean, or Lanka, or the words I went, Rama would have spent every sentence waiting, heart in his throat. If he had begun with her name alone, Rama might have braced for the worst. Seen comes first, and the fear is answered before it can rise. The Tamil poet Kamban, retelling the story, makes it even sharper: his Hanuman opens with the Tamil for I saw, before he names her at all. Only then does Hanuman tell the rest: the leap, the city at night, the ashoka grove, a thin woman under a tree, Ravana's threats, Rama's own ring passed down through the branches. Joy comes over Rama and Lakshmana as they listen. Sugriva had already guessed, from the monkeys' wild celebration on the way home. It's one word in a very long epic, but it shows who Hanuman is. He can leap an ocean. Here his greatness is quieter: before he speaks, he thinks about where his words will land. He arranges his sentence around someone else's fear.
screen: `DRISHTA: SEEN.` · `THE FEAR ANSWERED FIRST.` · `KAMBAN'S HANUMAN: I SAW.` · then, large: `HE ARRANGES HIS WORDS AROUND RAMA'S FEAR.`

segments.voice: Think of one piece of news you'll bring to someone soon, a result, a plan, a change, and ask Hanuman's question: what's the fear on their side, and what would they need to hear first so the rest lands softly? Find that first word, and just hold it with the breath; you don't have to say it yet.
Seen. Drishta in Sanskrit. Hanuman's first word to Rama, put first on purpose, so the fear is over before the story begins.
Your line: he arranges his words around Rama's fear. Tomorrow, what he carried back in his hand. Day six hundred thirty-two, done.

howItsDone: Ramayana teachers, in temples and in family readings, often pause on Hanuman's first word, seen, as a lesson in how to speak; Kamban's Tamil Ramayana gives the same moment as I saw.

chat.says: Why does it matter that Hanuman said seen before anything else?
options: It answered Rama's fear first, so the rest of the story could land softly.
It showed off his skill as a poet in front of the whole army.
It was a secret password Rama had given to all the searchers.
chat.meaning: Had Hanuman begun with the journey, or her name alone, Rama would have waited in fear. Seen comes first, so the fear is answered before it rises.

notes: The index word is the title's head, written exactly as the index gives it ("seen, with the opening quotation mark); the outline may want the word set to seen or dṛṣṭā.
Valmiki's exact wording of the first report (dṛṣṭā devī / dṛṣṭā sīteti) and its sarga in the vulgate numbering: confirm. The script says only that drishta, seen, comes first.
Kamban's Hanuman opening with kaṇṭaṉeṉ (I saw) is paraphrased, not quoted; confirm the reference and the twelfth-century dating.
Rama waits on Mount Prasravana near Kishkindha; the script says only 'a mountain outside Kishkindha'.
Sugriva's guess (from the monkeys' wild celebration in the honey grove) is told briefly; day 631 tells it in full, so this is a one-line recap.
